To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of shift work are complex, with a range of positive, neutral and negative effects on health.
shift workers are at increased risk for a variety of medical disorders.
the health of shift workers may be compromised by a range of disorders including coronary heart disease, peptic ulcer disease and compromised pregnancy outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people can be helped to cope more effectively with the effects of shift work, and to avoid or reduce the risk of the medical disorders associated with this type of work.
the development and evaluation of new and existing methods for the assessment and treatment of chronic pain.
understanding the mechanisms underlying these associations and with identifying the factors which modify the relationship between shift work and ill health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is not sufficient to establish a causal link between shift work and any specific disease.
shift workers are more likely to have a range of disorders and that these disorders are more severe than in day workers.

there is an increased risk of peptic ulcer disease and pregnancy problems in shift workers, a possible increased risk of coronary heart disease and an increased risk of some types of accidents in shift workers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

shift work is associated with an increased risk of peptic ulcer disease (especially in those with Helicobacter pylori infection), coronary heart disease, compromised pregnancy outcome, breast cancer, and possibly diabetes mellitus.
shift workers are at greater risk of developing peptic ulcer disease and coronary heart disease, but that the magnitude of this risk is small.

shift work is a significant risk factor for peptic ulcer disease and coronary heart disease, that the evidence is less clear for the other disorders and that the evidence is insufficient for some disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to do more research to understand the impact of shift work on human health.
shift workers are a vulnerable population that needs special care.
the health of shift workers is not just about sleep, but rather it is about the quality of sleep, the quality of the shift, and the quality of life.
